findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a `datetime`, so even the first optimized request reaches this method while building its cursor and raises TypeError. Authorized users requesting `optimized_pagination=true` will receive a 500 instead of an audit-log page. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible timestamp conversion (or needs to inherit from DateTimePaginator).

findings.title: Advertised negative cursor offsets cause Django queryset failures
findings.body: The advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing with ValueError rather than interpreting it as reverse pagination. Since cursor offsets are parsed from client input, an authorized caller can trigger a 500 using a negative offset; this does not provide the claimed bidirectional pagination behavior. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a valid ranged query.

findings.title: Changing live span keys from sets to sorted sets has no migration path
findings.body: This now executes ZADD against `span-buf:s:*` keys, while deployed versions created these keys as Redis sets. During a rolling deployment, any active buffered trace with a pre-existing set will make ZADD fail with WRONGTYPE (and later ZSCAN/ZCARD and the Lua script will fail similarly). A single such key can fail the pipeline/batch and prevent span processing until the old key expires, losing or delaying spans. Use a versioned key namespace or explicitly migrate/handle legacy set keys before issuing sorted-set commands.

findings.title: Lua eviction bypasses the configurable segment-size limit
findings.body: The script unconditionally retains only 1,000 members, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` remains a constructor option and was previously enforced by `_load_segment_data`. Configurations below 1,000 are no longer honored (oversized segments are emitted rather than rejected), and configurations above 1,000 silently lose spans. The configured limit needs to be passed to the script and used for eviction, or the obsolete option and its contract need to be removed consistently.

findings.title: Reducing redirect traversal depth can split valid deep traces
findings.body: Redirect resolution was reduced from 10,000 links to 1,000. For a trace whose parent chain exceeds 1,000 spans and arrives out of order, the loop stops before reaching the existing segment root, stores the span under an intermediate key, and produces separate/incomplete segments. The prior code explicitly documented the depth limit as the condition under which trees can fail to merge; lowering it is a functional regression unless ingestion guarantees a maximum depth of 1,000.
